chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning disciplining the child and the owned servant. He said: “Five or six, and be gentle.”

key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: the child being trained or disciplined
key_terms.خَمْسَةٌ: five; a stated limit in discipline
key_terms.سِتَّةٌ: six; an upper count mentioned in discipline
key_terms.وَارْفُقْ: and be gentle; show leniency and softness

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about disciplining a child or servant?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a brief legal-ethical guideline about disciplining a child or an owned servant, setting a limited measure and commanding gentleness. Its significance lies in combining restraint with compassion, indicating that correction must not exceed bounds and should be done with leniency.
